stories.title: Sustainability reporting remains a challenge for European firms
stories.summary: Central European companies are struggling to link sustainability disclosures with financial outcomes in their second year of reporting under the CSRD. A Deloitte study found that only 7% of analyzed firms disclosed quantitative data on current financial effects, while 4% quantified anticipated impacts. Data is elusive.

stories.title: Investment managers seek clarity in sustainability data
stories.summary: Simplifying sustainability reporting is not the same as making information easier to use. Investment managers in the UK and EU face a challenge in collecting and comparing data reliably. The industry is currently navigating a complex regulatory landscape while rethinking its own reporting obligations and data requirements.

stories.title: Deloitte Switzerland releases 2026 sustainability report
stories.summary: Deloitte Switzerland has published its latest sustainability report, incorporating European Sustainability Reporting Standards for the first time. The firm notes that clients are currently focused on responding to changing business conditions and generating value from AI. The report details the firm's investments in people and technology.

stories.title: Guardian Media Group reports progress on emissions targets
stories.summary: Guardian Media Group has published its 2025/26 sustainability report, noting an 8% reduction in emissions over the past year. The company aims to cut emissions by 67% by 2030. Print operations currently account for just under 60% of the group's total carbon footprint, down from 73% in 2020.

stories.title: Corporate social impact reporting lacks credible metrics
stories.summary: Companies frequently report on volunteer hours and donations but struggle to prove these interventions change anything. A new analysis reveals a widespread inability to track real outcomes of corporate responsibility. Justification for social budgets remains built on faith rather than evidence of impact on the ground.

stories.title: MetLife 2025 Sustainability Report - Markets Group
UK firms face sustainability reporting readiness gap
stories.summary: Listed companies must meet new UK Sustainability Reporting Standards, yet many boards remain unaware of their foundational vulnerabilities. Fragmented data across departments threatens to expose shortcomings during upcoming cycles. Organizations are now being urged to evaluate whether their internal controls can withstand investor skepticism and independent assurance requirements.

stories.title: EU consults on sustainability reporting assurance
stories.summary: The EU has launched a consultation on standards for the independent review of sustainability reports. Large companies are required to report under the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, and this process, known as assurance, is intended to ensure the information provided is credible for investors and other stakeholders.

stories.title: Dürr Group receives sustainability reporting award
stories.summary: The Dürr Group has been awarded the Building Public Trust Award 2026 for transparent and credible reporting. An independent jury praised the company for integrating sustainability into its corporate strategy. The award recognizes the firm's efforts to combine economic and environmental benefits for its customers.

stories.title: Juventus outlines sustainability data management
stories.summary: Juventus has detailed its processes for collecting and validating sustainability information. The club uses its Consolidated Sustainability Statement to communicate ESG policies and performance to stakeholders. These oversight mechanisms have been structured over time as part of a journey that began in the 2013/2014 football season.

stories.title: Juventus adopts CSRD framework for sustainability reporting
stories.summary: Juventus has published its 13th sustainability report, adopting the European Sustainability Reporting Standards for the second consecutive year. The club is the only Italian football team to use this framework, which is integrated into its annual financial report and subject to independent assurance. The reporting is rigorous.

stories.title: FRC demands more detail on stewardship accountability
stories.summary: The Financial Reporting Council has called for greater transparency in stewardship reports. A review of reporting under the revised UK code suggests that signatories should provide more information regarding how they scrutinize external managers. The regulator is seeking improved detail on accountability.

stories.title: Debate continues over voluntary carbon market accounting
stories.summary: The debate over whether host countries should apply corresponding adjustments to carbon credits remains unresolved. Proponents argue these accounting entries prevent double counting, while others fear they could shrink the market. The result determines whether the market becomes more credible or less effective for climate finance.

stories.title: Oasification proposed as nature-based carbon removal
stories.summary: Oasification aims to reverse desertification by improving how drylands capture and retain water. The approach focuses on allowing vegetation to recover and ecosystems to become healthier. Beyond environmental benefits, proponents suggest the method could create new opportunities for carbon removal projects and nature-based finance in the future.

stories.title: COP31 focuses on carbon market effectiveness
stories.summary: Negotiators at COP31 are discussing how to increase climate finance for developing countries as global warming exceeds the 1.5 C target. Carbon markets are being positioned as a potential solution to help companies and countries offset emissions. Adaptation remains a priority as climate risks increase globally.

stories.title: Carbon capture eyed for EU border tariff compliance
stories.summary: Industry experts at COP31 are examining how carbon capture and storage could help exporters meet EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism requirements. Türkiye, which sends 40% of its exports to the EU, is under pressure to decarbonize. International cooperation and regulatory alignment are cited as necessary for commercial viability.

stories.title: UN moves to implement Article 6.4 carbon market
stories.summary: The UN has approved the first credits under the Article 6.4 mechanism, a centralized system for generating and selling carbon credits under the Paris Agreement. While early signs suggest the rules will be stringent, the work of establishing a framework to restore market confidence is still ongoing.

stories.title: Philippines joins coalition to grow carbon markets
stories.summary: The Philippines has joined the Coalition to Grow Carbon Markets to expand its national framework. Environment Secretary Juan Miguel T. Cuna stated that private investment must complement public finance to accelerate climate action. The move aligns with the country's existing executive orders on sustainable development.

stories.title: UK cement imports shift as EU carbon rules take effect
stories.summary: Importers are redirecting cement shipments to the UK following the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. Non-EU imports reached 29.3 percent of the total by September 2026, up from 17.1 percent the previous year. The UK does not implement its own equivalent carbon border tax until 2027.

stories.title: Singapore and Kenya sign carbon trading agreement
stories.summary: Kenya and Singapore have signed a bilateral agreement to transfer carbon credits under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement. The framework aims to open channels for international climate finance, allowing Kenyan projects to supply emissions credits to Singapore-based companies seeking to meet their climate targets.

stories.title: Why COP31 could be quietly consequential for carbon markets - Sustainable Views
Non-EU cement imports to UK hit record high
stories.summary: Non-EU countries accounted for 29 percent of UK cement imports in the first nine months of 2026, the highest level since records began in 2000. The Mineral Products Association attributes the shift to the EU's carbon border tax, which encourages suppliers to avoid the bloc until 2027.

stories.title: Philippines joins global coalition to grow carbon markets
stories.summary: The Philippines has joined 17 other countries in the Coalition to Grow Carbon Markets. Announced at COP31, the membership aims to strengthen carbon trading and attract private investment for climate action. The country also endorsed a statement urging policies that stimulate demand for credible carbon credits.

stories.title: Norway Signs 10-Year Carbon Credit Deals With Morocco and Indonesia - Barlaman Today
EU endorses global electrification pledge
stories.summary: The European Union has backed a COP31 pledge to increase the share of electricity in global final energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035. The initiative, launched by the Turkish presidency, is presented by the EU as an efficient path to transition away from fossil fuels.

stories.title: Climate change health risks included in COP31 draft
stories.summary: The first draft of the COP31 political decision includes a paragraph on the risks of climate change to human health. It highlights threats from heat stress, food insecurity, and climate-sensitive diseases like malaria, marking a symbolic inclusion for advocates seeking to integrate health into UN climate processes.

stories.title: Tensions rise over COP31 draft climate deal
stories.summary: A draft cover decision published by Australia has sparked disagreement at the COP31 summit. The text includes calls for a fossil fuel phaseout, which the EU climate envoy described as needing significant change. Delegates remain divided as negotiations continue toward the end of the conference.

stories.title: COP31 negotiations stall as positions entrench
stories.summary: A senior expert from the United Nations University Institute for Environment and Human Security reports that participating countries are not yet moving toward consensus at COP31. Instead, nations are becoming entrenched in their positions, a development described as normal for this stage of the conference.

stories.title: Countries announce fossil fuel transition roadmaps
stories.summary: Denmark, Luxembourg, Portugal, Spain, and the Blue Pacific have announced roadmaps to transition away from fossil fuels. Oil Change International stated these plans send a signal to the COP31 presidencies that the transition should not be sidelined in the fine print of the final negotiations.

stories.title: COP31 Day 9: Negotiations Continue, While Super Pollutant Action Focuses on Implementation and Investment - Climate and
EU climate chief focuses on implementation at COP31
stories.summary: EU Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra stated the bloc is attending COP31 with a focus on delivering existing climate commitments rather than new pledges. Hoekstra noted that financial resources alone cannot address the climate crisis without concrete action and implementation of current goals.

stories.title: EU prioritizes existing pledges over new commitments
stories.summary: Irish Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien confirmed the EU is prioritizing the implementation of existing climate commitments at COP31. While the bloc welcomed the early release of a draft cover decision, O’Brien noted that the EU holds reservations regarding several proposals contained within the initial text.

stories.title: COP31 draft calls for immediate fossil fuel transition
stories.summary: A draft deal at COP31 calls for an immediate transition away from fossil fuels and a tripling of climate adaptation finance to $120 billion. The text also includes a target to increase global electrification to 35 percent by 2035, an approach that has proven divisive among delegates.

stories.title: First draft of COP31 deal signals tough negotiations to come - Reuters
COP31 president defends early draft text
stories.summary: Australia's climate minister Chris Bowen stated that the early release of a draft cover decision is a genuine attempt to draw out parties on their areas of agreement. The text includes contentious proposals, such as an immediate transition away from fossil fuels, with four days of negotiations remaining.

stories.title: CIWM and CEI launch circular economy vision for 2050 at COP31
stories.summary: CIWM and the Circular Economy Institute have launched a vision for 2050 at COP31, outlining four scenarios for the resources sector. The report, commissioned by CIWM’s Policy and Innovation Forum, aims to support UK resource security and economic growth. The future is now categorised into four distinct paths.

stories.title: Colruyt to sell 10,000 exclusive Trappist beer boxes
stories.summary: From 18 November, Colruyt will sell 10,000 gift boxes containing six Trappist beers, including the elusive Westvleteren Blond. The beer is typically available only at Saint-Sixtus Abbey, with this being its first supermarket appearance since 2011. The abbey's beer has a reputation for being difficult to acquire.

stories.title: Cotton Incorporated summit calls for reliable sustainability data
stories.summary: Cotton Incorporated gathered industry representatives in San Diego to discuss sustainability challenges. Discussions focused on lower-impact farming and soil health, with participants identifying a common need for reliable data. The industry is reportedly ready to move from conversation to action, provided the measurements are accurate.

stories.title: Schwalbe reports 20.8 million recycled tires and tubes
stories.summary: German manufacturer Schwalbe has processed 20.8 million bicycle tires and tubes through its recycling system. The company’s 2025/2026 sustainability report also notes progress in fair-trade rubber sourcing and greenhouse gas reductions. The program aims to recover materials from components that have reached the end of their life.

stories.title: JEC Composites Sustainability Report 2026: from innovation to industrial-scale production and integration throughout the
Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets adopts COP31 declaration
stories.summary: The Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets adopted a declaration in Antalya to coordinate international carbon market cooperation. Chaired by Brazil with China and the EU, the coalition launched working groups to set priorities for 2027. The group aims to become a key reference point for carbon pricing.

stories.title: Rwanda showcases 29 carbon projects at COP31
stories.summary: Rwanda has registered 29 carbon market projects and launched a new registry and renewable energy fund at COP31. The country previously reported $1.5 million in credit sales, with prices ranging from $14 to $45 per tonne. The projects span sectors including forestry, waste management and electric mobility.

stories.title: Ghana promotes carbon market model at COP31
stories.summary: Ghana has authorised the transfer of 34,705 carbon credits to Switzerland under an Article 6 cookstove initiative. Environment Minister Dr. Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings offered to lead a peer-learning programme to help other African nations develop similar registry and authorisation systems. The country is positioning its experience as a regional model.

stories.title: Ghana offers carbon market roadmap to African nations
stories.summary: Ghana has offered to share its experience in carbon credit generation and transfer with other African countries. The initiative aims to support the development of national systems for measuring and authorising emissions reductions. The offer was made during the African Ministerial Conference on the Environment in Antalya.

stories.title: COP31 addresses the climate cost of AI infrastructure
stories.summary: Discussions at COP31 have turned to the physical footprint of artificial intelligence. Data centres require significant electricity, land and grid capacity to support cooling and server operations. The challenge remains how to expand infrastructure without increasing carbon emissions. The digital world is proving to be quite heavy.

stories.title: Sabey Data Centers signs 10-year Texas solar agreement
stories.summary: Sabey Data Centers has signed a 10-year agreement for 43.5 megawatts of capacity from the Greasewood solar project in Texas. The deal secures an estimated 130 gigawatt-hours of renewable electricity annually to support the company’s 2029 net-zero goal. The agreement does not involve direct physical delivery of electricity.

stories.title: Alibaba signs Antalya AI pledge as US tech firms abstain
stories.summary: Alibaba is the only major technology company to sign the UN-backed Antalya AI Pledge, which drew 90 endorsements. Large US firms have not joined the voluntary agreement. The gap is notable for researchers, as the cloud infrastructure behind climate and AI research is largely controlled by the absent companies.

stories.title: Amazon targets $7 billion in Indian renewable energy by 2030
stories.summary: Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030, adding to its existing $4 billion commitment. The company also announced a target to cut the carbon intensity of its global electricity use by 65% by 2030. It remains a large corporate purchaser of energy.

stories.title: Amazon adds 934 MW of wind and solar capacity in India
stories.summary: Amazon has announced four new wind and solar projects in India with a combined capacity of 934 megawatts. The company’s total planned and contracted spending on clean power in India now reaches $11 billion. The largest project is a 234 megawatt wind farm located in Karnataka.

stories.title: Air India and Airbus partner on sustainable aviation fuel
stories.summary: Air India and Airbus have signed a feasibility study agreement to develop a voluntary corporate sustainable aviation fuel programme in India. The framework aims to allow businesses to reduce lifecycle emissions from air travel. The agreement was signed in the presence of the Minister of Civil Aviation.

stories.title: Google signs first superhot geothermal power agreement
stories.summary: Google has signed a power purchase agreement with Quaise to buy carbon-free energy from a superhot geothermal project in Oregon. The facility is expected to begin operations by 2030. Quaise uses a millimeter-wave drilling system to harness heat from deep below the surface to generate electricity.

stories.title: UL Solutions to acquire Worldly for $350 million
stories.summary: UL Solutions has agreed to acquire supply chain data platform Worldly for $350 million. The platform hosts the Higg Index, a suite of sustainability tools for the fashion industry. UL Solutions stated the acquisition is intended to strengthen its supply chain intelligence and software growth strategy.

stories.title: India and Sweden launch LeadIT 3.0 at COP31
stories.summary: India and Sweden have launched the third phase of the LeadIT coalition, focusing on net-zero transformations in steel and cement. Brazil has joined as the newest member. The 2027 to 2030 mandate shifts the initiative’s focus from building partnerships to scaling projects and mobilizing capital for hard-to-abate sectors.

stories.title: Inditex joins 250 million dollar fund for supply chain decarbonization
stories.summary: Inditex, the owner of Zara, is an anchor investor in the new 250 million dollar Decarbonization of Textile, Apparel, and Footwear Suppliers fund. Managed by SIMA and the IFC, the initiative aims to finance energy efficiency and pollution reduction projects. The fashion industry is now funding its own footprint.

stories.title: Global Energy Storage Alliance launched at COP31
stories.summary: The Global Energy Storage Alliance launched at the China Pavilion during COP31 in Antalya. Established by the China Energy Storage Alliance and other industry stakeholders, the platform aims to enhance international cooperation on power system flexibility. The alliance has arrived to discuss the role of storage.

stories.title: Local ballot contests show resistance to data centre expansion
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has identified AI as a priority for Britain's 2027 G20 presidency. However, voters in the US recently favoured limits on data centre development in 40 of 41 local ballot contests. National AI ambitions are currently meeting local infrastructure concerns.

research.summary: India’s objective should not be to turn outer space into another arena of conflict, but to ensure that disruption in space does not translate into vulnerability on Earth. India needs a comprehensive doctrine on space security

research.summary: The pilot demonstrations will cover Bengaluru and Shimla, and the deliverables will include the horizontal and vertical dimensions of urban settlements, offering a more comprehensive understanding of how Indian cities are expanding and densifying.
